title: The conormal module of a presentation injects into that of its principal localization
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $P=A[x_s,\ s\in S]$ a polynomial ring over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\alpha:P\to B$ a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras with kernel $I$; $I/I^2$ is a $B=P/I$-module. Let $g\in B$, let $B_g$ be the localization of $B$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], let $P[x]$ be the polynomial ring over $P$ in one further variable $x$, and let $\beta:P[x]\to B_g$ be the homomorphism of $A$-algebras which is $\alpha$ followed by $B\to B_g$ on $P$ and sends $x$ to $1/g$, with kernel $J$. Then $\beta$ is surjective, so $J/J^2$ is a module over $P[x]/J\cong B_g$, and the $B_g$-linear map $$\iota:(I/I^2)\otimes_BB_g\longrightarrow J/J^2,\qquad (a\bmod I^2)\otimes b\longmapsto b\cdot(a\bmod J^2)\quad(a\in I\subseteq J,\ b\in B_g),$$ is injective.
